title: The steward who drifted alone for 133 days
hook: One sailor drifted alone on a raft for one hundred thirty-three days.
summary: After a U-boat sank his ship in 1942, steward Poon Lim survived 133 days alone on a raft by making a fishhook, collecting rain and staying fit, until Brazilian fishermen found him.
sources: Wikipedia: Poon Lim - SS Benlomond sunk 23 Nov 1942 by U-172; 133 days adrift; rescued April 1943 by Brazilian fishermen; awarded British Empire Medal
Guinness World Records / Royal Museums Greenwich accounts of Poon Lim's survival on a raft, including improvised fishing hooks and rainwater

lines.text: One sailor drifted alone on a raft for one hundred thirty-three days.
lines.caps: One *sailor | alone on a *raft | for *133 days

lines.text: In nineteen forty-two, a German submarine sank his ship.
Poon Lim, a Chinese steward, climbed onto a wooden raft alone.
The biscuits and water slowly ran low.
So he bent a hook, and began catching fish.
lines.caps: So he bent a *hook, | and caught *fish

lines.text: He collected rain, and swam daily to stay strong.
Ships passed by without ever seeing him.
Finally, in April nineteen forty-three, Brazilian fishermen spotted him.
It is still the longest time adrift on record.

post.caption:
He made a fishhook on a raft and lived 133 days at sea.
Could you have lasted even one week?
